Title: Contract

For your contract project you need parts from several web shops.
In order to find out which web shop has the right parts, you have to query them all, and find out how much they can deliver, at which price, and how long it will take.
Create a list of parts that you order from each shop.
If one shop has not enough  parts, order from several shops.
Always use the cheapest parts.
The parts arrive in batches in a random order, typically they are +/- 2 days earlier/later.
When the first parts arrive you start building.
Sometimes you have to reorder parts.
If your stock (for a single part) falls below 5, you reorder (the cheapest), if it falls below 3 you reorder again (the fastest).
If it is zero, you write a mail to your friends, complaining about the webshops.

result.process_description:
Title: Contract

For your contract project you need parts from several web shops.
In order to find out which web shop has the right parts, you have to query them all, and find out how much they can deliver, at which price, and how long it will take.
Create a list of parts that you order from each shop.
If one shop has not enough  parts, order from several shops.
Always use the cheapest parts.
The parts arrive in batches in a random order, typically they are +/- 2 days earlier/later.
When the first parts arrive you start building.
Sometimes you have to reorder parts.
If your stock (for a single part) falls below 5, you reorder (the cheapest), if it falls below 3 you reorder again (the fastest).
If it is zero, you write a mail to your friends, complaining about the webshops.

args.text: When a process description says that goods or other items arrive asynchronously, in batches, or in an unpredictable order, model their arrival as an event that triggers subsequent work rather than as a task to wait for or receive them.

result.rule: Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.
Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
Use bpmn:sendTask or bpmn:receiveTask when sending or waiting for a message is itself the modeled unit of work.
Do not merge separately described actions into one task or split one stated action without a process reason. Preserve described dependencies.

args.text: When a description says items arrive asynchronously, in batches, or in an unpredictable order, model their arrival as an intermediate catch event that triggers subsequent work, rather than as a task to wait for or receive them.

result.rule: When the description says that the process waits for a stated time or period to end before continuing: Model the wait as an intermediate catch timer event, then connect it to the subsequent activity rather than representing the passage of time as a task.

When the description states that a participant’s response or communication causes the process to continue to subsequent work: Label the corresponding intermediate catch event as the receipt or occurrence of that response, rather than as an action performed by the participant.

When the description states that a notification or milestone can occur after process work has begun: Model the later trigger within the ongoing process as an intermediate catch event, not as an independent process start event.

When the description says that a process may continue only after an external participant approves a proposal: Model the approval wait as an intermediate catch event after the proposal is provided and before the dependent activity; preserve that order rather than modeling the wait as a task.

args.text: When the description says that items are delivered in batches and subsequent work depends on their arrival: Model the relevant arrival as an intermediate catch event that triggers that work, rather than as a task for waiting for or receiving the items.
